findings.title: Silent `''` fallback when a view has no projectPath
findings.description: `viewRoot` returns `stripTrailingSeparator(view.view.projectPath ?? '')`. If a view ever lacks a `projectPath`, `fixRelPath` computes `relative('', abs)`, which resolves against the process cwd. `gateByReadiness` and `commitViewWrites` would then run git against a root of `''`. Project rules forbid silent fallback values. `check.ts` and `workflowTools.ts` guard only the invoking path, not each view's root. Throw an explicit error when a view's `projectPath` is missing. `fixOwnership.ts` already handles the same case by returning `null`.

findings.title: Git failures misclassified as NOT_A_CHECKOUT / DETACHED_HEAD
findings.description: The `catch {}` around `rev-parse --show-toplevel` maps every failure to `NOT_A_CHECKOUT`. That includes a `FIX_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` timeout, a spawn error, or a lock problem. The `symbolic-ref -q` catch likewise maps every failure to `DETACHED_HEAD`. The comments justify the expected exit codes, but the catches are not narrowed to them. The user would be told a worktree is "missing" or "detached" when git simply hung or errored. Inspect the error's exit code and rethrow or defer with a distinct reason for anything else. The `DeferredFix.detail` field could carry the text.

findings.title: Duplicated scope/invoking-checkout orchestration between CLI and MCP
findings.description: `workflowTools.ts` repeats the scope-view construction (the `fileSlice: \`${n}-slice\`` overlay), the `runCheck` selection, the `resolveInvokingCheckout` call and the plan-then-apply sequence from `check.ts:172-198` and `runRoutedFix`. The `-slice` suffix literal and the "multi → resolve invoking checkout" rule now live in two places and can drift. The existing comments already say the merge logic is shared so it cannot drift. Move `scopeViews`/`runCheck` and the invoking-checkout resolution into `@context-forge/core`, next to `planRoutedFixes`.

findings.title: Test code reaches across packages into core's test directory
findings.description: The CLI and MCP tests import `../../../core/tests/helpers/gitWorktreeFixture.js` by relative path. That couples package test trees and depends on tsconfig `include` and build exclusion. A refactor in core's `tests/` breaks the other packages silently. Publish the fixture as a dev-only workspace test-utils package or export, or keep a shared `tests/` location outside any single package.

findings.title: Unused exports and out-of-order helper in routedFixes.test.ts
findings.description: `designPath`, `tasksPath`, `completeBeta`, `worktreeCtx`, `createRoutedSetup`, `dryRun`, `aboutSubject` and `RoutedSetup` are `export`ed. A grep of `packages/**/tests` shows no other file imports them. `createProjectFor` is declared at the bottom and reads module-level `setup`. Drop the `export`s, or move the helpers to `tests/helpers` if they are meant to be shared. Make `createProjectFor` take the base project as a parameter.

findings.title: Human text can reach stdout under `--json` when nothing is fixable
findings.description: In the all-slices path with zero fixable findings, `runRoutedFix` calls `printCheckOutput` and `console.log(dim(...))` before returning `null`, regardless of `opts.json`. A JSON consumer gets prose instead of a result object. The same shape existed before this change for explicit `--fix`, so it is not a regression. It now also covers `workflow.auto_fix`, so it is worth fixing while the function is being reworked.

findings.title: Previously `fix`/`fixAll` are now unreachable from production code
findings.description: A grep of `packages/**/src` finds no `.fix(` or `.fixAll(` callers after the CLI and MCP moved to `planRoutedFixes` + `applyFixPlan`. The methods still exist and now return empty `deferred`/`commits`. Confirm whether they are public API. If not, remove them, since they bypass the ownership routing this change introduces.

findings.title: Fix ownership, deferral and commit flow
findings.description: Ownership resolution is a pure function with a table-driven test. `DeferReason` uses an `as const` map with a compile-time exhaustive label table, and a test asserts every reason has a label. Commits are path-scoped and run no `--no-verify`. A failed commit restores the written paths and defers them rather than leaving partial writes. Readiness is re-checked after the prompt. Single-checkout runs are asserted to spawn no git process. `subjectIndex` is a required field set from parsed indices, never from labels.
